brief: A D2-symmetric 64x64 border tile with period 16 along the horizontal axis: a saw-tooth outer edge, a row of double-outlined fish-eye circles, and all enclosed regions filled with parallel hatching at 3 px pitch; four inks (black, turmeric, vermilion, indigo) on a rice-paper ground.
A brick-red tile with a single stepped white hexagon centred on it and a yellow dot at its core.
A cream-ground tile with six overlapping red circles around a central circle, each circle drawn as a white-red-black triple line.

A 64x64 Ilkal-inspired tile: 8-px period indigo pin-stripes on mustard across the body, a 16-px red right-hand border carrying the tope-teni sequence white-red-white-red-white (widths 2-3-6-3-2, mirror-symmetric), and a 2-px peacock-green line separating body and border; five colours max.

A 64x64 kasavu-inspired tile: plain cream field, bottom border sequence gold-cream-red-cream-gold with widths 4-2-6-2-4 px, mirrored onto the opposite edge to satisfy the host symmetry; a 1-px green line at each outer edge; three accent colours plus cream, and translation symmetry along x.
An off-white tile with a black checker (choukari) lattice and a small red diamond in every cell.
A sparse white-on-ochre tile with a centered square outlined by a dotted line and four small triangles at the corners.
A black tile with a bottom border strip mirrored onto the opposite edge to satisfy the host symmetry, made of four concentric red-and-white diamonds on an 8x8 cell grid.
A white tile with a central pair of red horizontal bands separated by a thin white line, a green line on each side, and a solid black band across each end.
A red tile with four equal black horizontal bands separated by thin red lines and a single centred row of small white squares.

A 64x64 counted grid (cell size 4) in madder red, black and white: a 9x9 saktapar chequerboard centred, framed by a 2-cell border of alternating white dots with translation period 2 cells, D4 symmetry overall, white limited to at most 20% of cells.

A Bawan-bagh-inspired counted-thread tile: a 64x64 field split into a 4x4 grid of 16-px squares, each square holding a D2-symmetric geometric fill from a set of at least four distinct patterns (nested lozenges, chevrons, zig-zag lines, dots), every mark on a 2-px stitch cell, square borders in yellow, ground visible only as 1-px outlines, maximum five colours including ground.

A 64x64 tile of 45-degree diagonal bands cycling through exactly five colours in the fixed order yellow, green, magenta, blue, white with widths 6,4,6,4,4 pixels, the pattern repeating with period 24 perpendicular to the bands and tiling seamlessly.

A stripe design inspired by Lepcha thara: groups of ten vertical stripes with a thick-thin-thin-thick width rhythm, ordered palette white-red-yellow-green-black repeated twice per group, and one band per group carrying a row of sideways chevrons with a 8 px period.

A 64x64 counted-thread panel inspired by Toda embroidery with a 16-cell period along x, three stacked bands (black zigzag, red lozenge chain, black zigzag), D2 symmetry within each period, only red and black on white, no mark off the 4x4 stitch cell, and at least 20% white background.

A black field with a vertical stripe sequence white(1)-red(3)-white(1)-black(4) repeating with period 9 and mirrored about the vertical midline, plus a single horizontal row of small white diamonds across the middle on a 3-cell grid, period 9; exactly three inks, black covering at least 50 percent.

A 64x64 counted grid (cell 4) with D4 symmetry: a central 8-point star, four corner kalka-like teardrops pointing inward, a wave border of period 8 cells, and every empty cell row carrying a running-stitch dash of period 2; four thread colours on a cream ground.
A two-tone plaited check on an 8-cell grid, alternating light and dark strips in both directions, mirror-symmetric.
A rust-red tile with a centred yellow lozenge and a white dot at each corner, on a 4-px stitch grid.
A white-on-brown tile with a centered square drawn in dots and a ring of eight small triangles around it.
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

brief: A jaali-inspired screen: hexagonal lattice of hexagonal holes with a six-pointed-star hole at the centre, D2 mirror symmetry, web thickness >= 3 px everywhere, one connected solid attached to a 4-px frame, 40-50% open area, two colours (sandstone and void).

A lattice inspired by Khatamband: a 64x64 panel of eight-pointed stars and interstitial squares with D4 symmetry, a single connected web at least 3 px wide everywhere, attached to a 4 px frame, repeating every 32 px in both axes.
A maroon field with a 4x4 lattice of small white rings, each with a maroon centre dot.

A counted-grid mat tile inspired by Lakshadweep coir weaves: a 4 px cell grid, a two-axis check in coir brown and cream with every fourth row replaced by a red-green stripe pair, a centred twill diamond with D2 symmetry, four colours maximum.

A kolam-inspired figure on a 5x5 square dot grid drawn as exactly two closed strokes that together enclose all 25 dots, with D4 symmetry, isolated crossings only, white on dark ground, and a wave-like outer ring of 8 equal lobes.
